title: CISNE REUNION
full_story:
Royalty was named last night at the Cisne Reunion, winning the Little Miss Pageant was Sarah Atwood, named Little Miss princess’s were Stella Troyer and Reese Simpson.  The retiring Little Miss is Maleah Lane, there were 10 contestants.

Lydia Atwood was named Junior Miss, 1st runner up was Aubrynn Barnfield and 2nd runner up was Eva Payne.  The retiring Junior Miss is Myla Hearle.  There were 7 contestants.

Esme Krupp was crowned Miss Cisne Reunion.    1st runner up was Abigail Baker and 2nd runner up was Kloyee Dagg.  The retiring Miss Cisne Reunion is Kaleya Porter, there were 7 contestants.

Tonight, in addition to Bingo from 7 to 9 pm, Jake Perry and Hayden Brown will take the stage in the park at 7 pm.

Tomorrow is a full day at the Cisne Reunion.  The day begins with race day registration and a community breakfast at the Community Center.  Race day Registration begins at 6 am on stage in the square, and the breakfast is from 7 to 10 am.

The 1 mile Fun Run is set to begin at 7:30 am, with the 15th annual 5K Run, Walk to begin at 8 am.  Tractor Show setup is from 8 to 10 am.  Car show registration begins at 9 am with awards at 12:30 pm, and the tractor show is at 10:30.  Kids’ Games and a FFA Petting Zoo on the square will be from 10 to Noon.  There will be a kids pedal pull at Noon on the square.  The annual parade lineup is at 2 pm at the high school with the parade at 2:30 pm.  Bill Atwood will serve as master of ceremonies for the Cisne Reunion parade.

The Ashes will perform from 4 to 6 pm, bingo will run from 5 to 9 pm and the Reunion closes with a performance by Duke Boys on the main stage at 7 pm.

The Cisne Masonic Lodge is grilling their World Famous Pork Chops and brats.  The lodge is located under the shelter on the south side of the square.  Sales will be during lunch today, evening events and all day Saturday.  This years Cisne Reunion event pays tribute to the Cisne High School Class of 1976 on their 50th reunion and the Class of 2001 on their 25th reunion.

title: MAIL IN BALLOTS
full_story:
Illinois voters can now apply to vote by mail for the November 3rd general election.

Illinois voters may request a mail-in ballot for any reason.  The deadline to request a ballot is October 29th.

Voters can request a mail-in ballot by completing an application.  Applications are available by visiting Clay County Clerk Amy Britton’s office in the Clay County Courthouse in person or through the Illinois State Board of Elections website.

Completed applications should be returned to the clerk’s office.

title: FFA STATE OFFICER TEAM CHOOSES THEME
full_story:
The Illinois FFA State Officer Team has selected “Legacy” as its theme for the 2026-27 year.

Announced July 27th by Illinois Association FFA, the theme honors the organization’s past and recognizes the impact current members can have on the future.  Illinois FFA will celebrate its 100th state convention in 2028, making the theme especially fitting as the organization looks ahead to its next century.

“We’re building a future for the FFA, continuing the organization,” said Illinois FFA State President Bryer Nelson.

Part of building the legacy has already begun for the six-member state officer team.  July 13th through 17th, the officers traveled to Washington, DC, for the National FFA State Officer Summit, joining state officers from across the country for leadership training.

They participated in advocacy training as well, which included discussions on career and technical education funding and meetings with lawmakers and congressional staff on Capitol Hill.  Officers also learned about the National FFA Caucus, a group of legislators that discusses agricultural education and the future of the ag industry.

Nelson said one of the biggest lessons from the experience was the importance of understanding the wide range of perspectives represented across Illinois FFA.

“There’s going to be a lot of different perspectives, a lot of different backgrounds,” Nelson said.  “We’re going to need to talk to the best farmers in Illinois and the people who have never stepped foot on farmland.”

Following DC, the officer team continued building leadership skills and connecting with members through a busy summer schedule.  Nelson attended the Illinois Coordinating Council for Career and Technical Student Organizations conference and participated in Illinois FFA Leadership Camp.

Nelson described camp, which welcomed FFA members to 4-H Memorial Camp in Monticello July 20th through 23rd, as a highlight of the summer.

“It was a lot of fun,” Nelson said.  “It was a great opportunity for some individuals in Illinois FFA.”

The state officer team will next represent the organization at the Illinois State Fair, August 13th through 23rd, one of the final major events of the summer before the school year begins.  Nelson said he is especially looking forward to working in the FFA Barnyard, where he previously spent time as both a visitor and section president.  Haven Cash, from the North Clay FFA serves as the State FFA Reporter.

title: SALES TAX HOLIDAY STARTS TODAY
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Revenue’s State Sales Tax Holiday for certain clothing and school-related items for back-to-school expenses starts today and runs through Sunday, August 16th.

The state sales tax holiday is a ten-day period during which consumers can purchase certain clothing and school-related items and pay sales tax at a reduced rate.  The state’s portion of sales tax due throughout the holiday is reduced by 5% from 6.25% to 1.25%.  Items include traditional supplies such as markers and pencils, notebooks and folders and other classroom items, as well as many clothing purchases.  Clothing items, including shoes, that cost less than $125 will qualify for a lower sales tax rate, while there will be no price limit on school supplies.

The last time the state approved such a program was in 2022, the last time JB Pritzker ran for reelection.

The sales tax holiday started today and ends on Sunday, August 16th.

title: FREEDOM CAUCUS STATEMENT
full_story:
A special House Committee convened Thursday to investigate the federal charges State Representative Carol Ammons is facing and it is clear Democrats have not taken to heart the lessons learned from the imprisonment of former House Speaker Mike Madigan, according to the Illinois Freedom Caucus.

“We are here because of years and years of unchecked one-party rule,” said State Representative Brad Halbrook.  “Sending the most powerful speaker of the House in the country to prison apparently was not enough of a wakeup call for Illinois Democrats who are continuing the same abuse of power that got Madigan into trouble in the first place.”

State Representative Chris Miller said the current protocols to safeguard ethical conduct are not working.

“Carol Ammons took the same ethics training, a video slideshow, we all took,” Miller said.  “Clearly, it did not work in her case.  Conversely, Harry Benton took sexual harassment training, another video slideshow, and that did not work either.  The reality we face is that decades of scandal have destroyed the public’s trust in state government.  This must end.”

While this is not a partisan issue, Halbrook said the Democrats have total control of the Capitol complex and must take ownership of the ethics problems emanating from their ranks.

“At some point, we have to be honest about who it is that is refusing to make the government more transparent, more ethical, and more accountable,” Halbrook said.  “The reason we do not have ethics reforms with real teeth is because Democrats refuse to pass them.  We can disagree about policy, politics, issues, but all 118 members of the House should conduct themselves ethically and morally.  The people of Illinois deserve reform in their government.  Those who refuse to do better should resign.”

title: BABY DELIVERED ON INTERSTATE
full_story:
A Jefferson County dispatcher helped guide a family through the delivery of a baby along Interstate 57.

The family was headed to Good Samaritan Hospital in Mount Vernon when labor progressed quickly.  Telecommunicator Haley Bressler gave childbirth instructions by phone while sending emergency crews.  Baby Georgia arrived before responders reached the scene.

The mother, baby and grandmother are doing well, and Bressler received a commendation from Sheriff Jeff Bullard.

title: NEW TRANSPARENCY LAW
full_story:
A new law sponsored by State Senator Jason Plummer will strengthen government transparency by making local audit and financial reports easier for Illinois residents to access.

“The people of Illinois deserve transparency when it comes to how units of government manage their tax dollars,” said Plummer.  “Public financial records should not be difficult to find or buried in websites.  This law is a simple, commonsense step to make important financial information easier for taxpayers to locate and review.”

House Bill 2137 requires local governments, counties, and municipalities that already maintain a public website to post information directing residents to where audit reports and financial statements can be accessed through the Illinois Comptroller’s Office.

“Improving access to these records strengthens accountability and gives residents the information they need to hold their local governments responsible,” added Plummer.

title: BRONCO RECALL
full_story:
Ford is recalling over 565-thousand Broncos to fix a fire safety risk.

The recall affects certain 2021 to 2026 Bronco and Bronco Raptor vehicles.  According to the recall paperwork, a short circuit in the engine bay may lead to smoke coming from the cabin air vents.  Drivers may also be notified of the issue with a warning message on the cluster.  The recall documents show that at the time of filing, Ford was aware of 15 incidents involving a fire that may have started with the engine compartment wiring harness.

Owners of affected vehicles will be notified and urged to bring their Bronco to a Ford dealership to have it serviced.  Dealer technicians will install convolute sheathing with abrasion tape to the wiring harness to prevent chafing and mitigate the risk of future short circuits.  Dealer notifications have already begun, with Ford planning to notify owners between August 24th and August 28th.

title: TRAM SERVICE AVAILABLE
full_story:
The Illinois State Fair announced the return of its most requested ride, the free tram.  The tram service is made possible through the support of the Illinois Corn Growers Association.  A dedicated daily route will be run by two trams throughout the 11 days of the fair.  Tram rides are free for all fairgoers and offer handicap accessibility.

“We want every guest to have a positive and accessible experience at the Illinois State Fair,” said Jerry Costello II, Director of the Illinois Department of Agriculture.  “The tram service helps visitors navigate the fairgrounds with ease, making it possible to enjoy countless exhibits, attractions, and events that make the fair a favorite summer tradition.”

Maps showing the tram routes will be displayed on the fairgrounds.  Trams will run from Noon to 8 pm on most weekdays and 10 am to 8 pm on weekends and on Monday, August 17th.

Stops include Happy Hollow at the Handicap Ramp to Illinois Building/Senior Center, Campground/Arena entrance, 4-H Road at the 4-H Master Gardens, entrance to Conservation World, Goat Barn at Grandstand Avenue, South End of the Half-Mile Track near Gate 4, ISF Security Office near the Fire Station, the Hobbies Arts & Crafts building, and just north of the Route 66 Experience at the new Surfside Social Club.

Wheelchair and scooter rentals are also available on the fairgrounds at the Senior Center inside the Illinois Building and on Grandstand Avenue near the Goat Barn.  Handicap parking is available at Gate 4, 7, and 11.

Mark your calendars for the 2026 Illinois State Fair, August 13th through August 23rd in Springfield.
